knobs.note: 0 makes the orchestrator's turn call no model at all: the primary turn (bin/claude-cost.sh, BH-2534) and the survival turn (bin/agent-call.sh) are both refused BEFORE the vendor call with a zero-cost row_source=refused row, and the orchestrator answers from its bash floor.

Comma/space list of the ONLY runners the orchestrator's turn may reach. Empty is every runner, i.e. today's ladder unchanged. The primary turn is runner claude (bin/claude-cost.sh); the survival turn names its own runner through bin/agent-call.sh. A runner outside the list is refused before the call.

Dollars the orchestrator's turns may spend in the current UTC day, summed from D1 cost_rows stamped lane_id=orc-monitor on stage orchestrator through GET /api/metrics/llm-spend, never from the box's own logs/cost.csv. Checked before both the primary (bin/claude-cost.sh) and the survival (bin/agent-call.sh) turn.

How many times bin/orchestrate.sh posts a turn's chat_reply ledger beat (BEAT_STRICT=1, rkey chat:<command id>) before it gives up and writes one ALERTS line naming the command id. Only turns with a console command id post. The retries run inside the turn (other turns run in parallel), so the worst case adds (tries-1) x backoff seconds plus each try's beat timeout to the turn.
Seconds slept between two chat_reply ledger beat attempts (none after the last). Bounded at 30 because the wait happens inside the turn (other turns run in parallel).

Characters of the reply text the chat_reply ledger beat carries; a longer reply is cut 120 characters short of this and ends with a cut marker. Telegram still gets the whole reply, and the full text is in /root/orchestrator/last-reply.txt.

1 makes the orchestrator ack the console command row with answered:<iso> (POST /api/commands/<id>/ack) after the reply leaves the turn. 0 sends no command-status ack; the chat_reply ledger beat still posts. The ack is fail-open: a failed POST is silent and never alerts.

BH-5336: how many orchestrator turns (bin/orchestrate.sh, one per chat message) run at once. A message starts its turn as soon as a slot is free; while it waits its command row says queued_behind:<oldest running id>. 0 = no configured cap: the cap is MemAvailable / ORC_TURN_WORKER_MEM_MB (1 to 32), like LEAD_REVIEW_BOX_MAX. Forced to 1 while flags/orchestrator-continue is active, because -c continues one shared claude conversation.
BH-5336: memory one orchestrator turn is sized at when ORC_TURN_CONCURRENCY is 0. The cap is then MemAvailable divided by this.

BH-5336: a turn claim ($ORC/state/turns/<key>.json) not touched by its heartbeat for this long is stale. The gate ignores it and a re-delivered copy of the command reclaims it. The heartbeat touches the claim every ORC_TURN_STALE_S/6 seconds while the turn's bash, or anything else in its process group, is alive.
